newsitem.title: UK: Iranian demand features in sugar freight inquiry.
newsitem.headline: Iranian demand features in sugar freight inquiry.

text.p: The sugar freight market saw a spate of fresh inquiry on Monday on fresh demand from Iran and neighbouring Iraq issued its first buying tender under the U.N. oil-for-food deal, shipbrokers said.
Shipbrokers said last week's three bagged orders from Louis Dreyfus were still open, as were Lorico's inquiry from Cuba to Syria and Czarnikow Rionda's African and US Gulf orders.
Iran again featured in the day's set of freight orders, as Aquarius quoted direct principals orders from UBC to ship two bagged cargoes for January shipment dates.
It quoted 14,000 tonnes from Antwerp-Hamburg range for January 1/15 and another 14,000 tonnes from Thailand for January 10/20.
Seabon was open on account for 14,000 tonnes min/max bagged sugar from the European Union excluding the U.K. to Iran for prompt/December 30 dates.
Elsewhere, Iraq tendered to buy between four and six cargoes of 100 ICUMSA white sugar on Tuesday for February/March shipment as part of the U.N. oil-for-food deal.
Confirming the market talk from Friday, Pakistan's state-run TCP scrapped its recent tender to buy 50,000 tonnes of crystal whites and reinvited bids for December 21 for delivery by January 11.
Benham quoted for 7,350 tonnes of bulk sugar from Belize to the US Gulf for December 28/January 5.
Seven Seas was in the market for 10/20,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from south Brazil to west Africa for December 25/30.

Lastly, Secretan quoted three new orders. It was in the market for 20/22,000 tonnes in bulk from Cuba to the Black Sea for January 15/20 and 6,000 from Marie Galante in Guadeloupe to Antwerp for January 31/onwards shipment dates.
Secretan was also open for 6,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from east coast Mexico to Nouakchott for December 20/27.
